literal: "They are young", "they are relatives", saying, they will not despise; with the standing splendor, to behave is fitting.
translation: One should not disrespect the ruler by thinking 'he is younger' or 'he is a relative.' Instead, one must conduct oneself in accordance with the enduring splendor of his position.
modern: இவர் என்னை விட வயதில் இளையவர் என்றோ, எனக்கு உறவினர் என்றோ அரசரை அவமதிக்கக் கூடாது. மாறாக, அரசப் பதவிக்கு உரிய நிலைத்த பெருமையோடு பொருந்தி நடப்பதே முறையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet advises on the proper decorum when serving a ruler who might be younger or related by blood. Familiarity or age differences should not lead to disrespect. The word 'ஒளி' (light or splendor) refers to the majesty and authority inherent in the ruler's position. Therefore, one must always act in accordance with that enduring royal dignity, setting aside personal familiarity.
